overview: Woodside Energy is a Perth-headquartered global oil and gas producer and Australia's largest LNG operator, with a portfolio spanning Australia (North West Shelf, Pluto, Bass Strait), Senegal (Sangomar), the US Gulf of America (Shenzi, Atlantis, Mad Dog), Mexico (Trion) and a major new LNG development under construction on the US Gulf Coast (Louisiana LNG). The company roughly doubled its production base and asset footprint via the June 2022 all-scrip merger with BHP's global petroleum business, becoming a top-10 global independent producer by volume and the largest energy company listed on the ASX. Woodside's strategy is to "thrive through the energy transition" by running a low-cost, cash-generative LNG/oil/domestic-gas base business while selectively investing in new energy products (ammonia, hydrogen, CCUS).

business_model.summary: Woodside earns revenue from producing and selling LNG, pipeline (domestic) gas, and oil/liquids/NGLs, largely under long-term offtake contracts and term LNG sale-and-purchase agreements (with an actively traded marketing/shipping arm), supplemented by shorter-cycle, high-cash-generation oil production. Revenue is inherently linked to global oil (Brent) and LNG (North East Asian spot/contract) prices, so it is transactional/commodity-price-driven rather than subscription-like, though long-dated LNG contracts (many indexed to oil with floors/ceilings) provide multi-year revenue visibility once signed.

revenue_streams.name: LNG (equity + marketing/trading)
revenue_streams.notes: Core franchise since Woodside pioneered Australian LNG in the 1980s (NWS, Pluto); set to grow materially with Scarborough (Q4 2026 first cargo) and Louisiana LNG (2029) additions

revenue_streams.name: Oil (Sangomar, Gulf of America, Trion from 2028)
revenue_streams.notes: High cash generation, short payback; Sangomar alone contributed $1.9bn Woodside-share revenue in FY2025; Trion targets first oil 2028

revenue_streams.name: Domestic/pipeline gas (Australia)
revenue_streams.notes: Steady, less commodity-cyclical cash flows supporting WA/east coast energy security

revenue_streams.name: New Energy (ammonia, hydrogen, CCUS)
revenue_streams.notes: Beaumont New Ammonia first production Dec-2025; targeting $5bn Scope 3 investment by 2030; immaterial revenue currently

business_model.customer_type: B2B — long-term LNG offtake with Asian/European utilities and trading houses (China Resources Gas, Uniper, PETRONAS, SK Gas, JERA, BOTAŞ among 2025 signings), oil sold into global spot/term markets, domestic gas sold to Australian industrial/utility customers
business_model.geographic_mix: Production/assets: Australia (NWS, Pluto, Bass Strait, Macedon), Senegal (Sangomar), US Gulf of America (Shenzi, Atlantis, Mad Dog, and under-construction Louisiana LNG), Mexico (Trion, under construction), Timor-Leste and Canada; FY2025 production 198.8 MMboe (115.3 MMboe gas / 83.5 MMboe liquids), record year driven by Sangomar reaching nameplate capacity

main_competitors: QatarEnergy / US Gulf Coast LNG developers (Cheniere, Venture Global)
competitive_position.market_position: Australia's largest LNG producer and one of the largest ASX-listed companies by market cap (~A$59-62bn); top-10 global independent E&P by production following the 2022 BHP merger; a top-tier but not dominant global LNG supplier relative to majors (Shell, TotalEnergies) who have larger, more diversified multi-basin LNG portfolios

moat_factors.description: Four decades of NWS/Pluto operating history, low unit production cost ($7.8/boe in FY2025) and record reliability (~98% operated LNG reliability) support a cost-advantaged position versus higher-cost global LNG supply

40-year record of reliable LNG delivery since first NWS cargo to Japan in 1989 underpins repeat long-term contracting (4.7 Mtpa of new LNG SPAs signed in 2025 alone) with major Asian and European utilities

Ability to attract infrastructure/financial partners (Stonepeak, Williams on Louisiana LNG; LNG Japan on Scarborough) to de-risk large capex and accelerate funding is a differentiator versus smaller peers
Integrated Pluto-KGP interconnector and shared infrastructure (NWS, Pluto, Scarborough) create processing flexibility and lower marginal development cost for future WA gas (e.g., Browse)
Baa1/BBB+ ratings and 10-20% gearing target support access to capital for growth, though negative outlook risk exists (S&P revised outlook to Negative post-Louisiana LNG FID)

weaknesses: No pricing power — a price-taker in global commodity markets for both oil and LNG
Smaller and less geographically diversified than supermajors (Shell, ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies) that can better absorb single-project setbacks
Heavy reliance on a handful of very large, multi-year capital projects (Scarborough, Trion, Louisiana LNG) for future growth, creating concentrated execution risk
Louisiana LNG has not yet secured offtake contracts for most of its expected production, unlike more contracted peers
Reputational/social-licence exposure given fossil-fuel core business amid activist and regulatory scrutiny of new approvals (e.g., past Scarborough legal challenges)

growth_drivers: Scarborough Energy Project (Australia) — 98% complete as of H1 2026, on budget, first LNG cargo targeted Q4 2026; adds a second Pluto LNG train and new low-cost WA supply

Louisiana LNG (US Gulf Coast) — positive FID taken April 2025, ~22-28% complete by mid-2026, targeting first LNG in 2029; positions Woodside as a 'global LNG powerhouse' able to serve both Pacific and Atlantic basins; capital intensity reduced via Stonepeak/Williams sell-downs (Woodside expected exposure <60% of total capex)
Trion oil project (Mexico, with PEMEX) — ~64% complete by mid-2026, targeting first oil 2028, diversifying into high-return, shorter-payback oil
Bass Strait operatorship transition from ExxonMobil (effective mid-2026) — expected to unlock further gas development and >US$60m of synergies via portfolio consolidation
Sangomar (Senegal) ramp — reached nameplate capacity in 2025, extended plateau production, demonstrating strong execution on the newest major asset
New long-term LNG offtake contracting momentum — 4.7 Mtpa signed in 2025 with China Resources Gas, Uniper, PETRONAS, SK Gas, JERA and BOTAŞ, evidencing durable demand ahead of new supply
New Energy optionality (Beaumont New Ammonia, hydrogen, CCUS) as a longer-dated but currently small growth/decarbonization option supporting Scope 3 targets
Secular LNG demand tailwind — Wood Mackenzie base case projects ~60% growth in global LNG demand to 2035, with coal-to-gas switching and firming of renewables as structural demand drivers

business.description: Scarborough, Trion and Louisiana LNG are large, multi-year, multi-billion-dollar projects exposed to cost overruns, schedule delays, supply chain constraints and skilled-labor shortages; Louisiana LNG in particular still lacks offtake contracts for most volumes
Woodside does not control operations, cost or pace at several non-operated interests (Bass Strait pre-transition, Wheatstone, Atlantis, Mad Dog); JV partners can exercise veto rights
Reserve estimates rely on judgment and can be revised downward, potentially triggering impairments or lower future production guidance

Long-serving CEO Meg O'Neill departed for BP (announced Dec-2025); Liz Westcott confirmed as permanent CEO in March 2026 after an acting period — execution continuity through major project completions is a near-term watch item

financial.description: Revenue, cash flow and asset valuations are directly exposed to Brent crude and LNG spot/contract prices; Dated Brent averaged US$69.1/bbl in 2025, down 14.4% YoY, and NPAT fell 24% in FY2025 largely on lower prices despite record production
FY2026 guided capex of $4.0-4.5bn (Scarborough, Trion, Louisiana LNG) plus the Beaumont completion payment; reliance on continued debt market access, asset sell-downs and partner capital
S&P revised outlook to Negative at Louisiana LNG FID, citing higher capex and portfolio risk; a downgrade would raise cost of capital

financial.risk: Foreign exchange and interest rate exposure
financial.description: USD reporting with AUD-denominated dividend/cost base creates translation exposure; floating-rate debt and deposits create interest rate sensitivity

regulatory.description: Major projects (Scarborough historically, Browse prospectively) face environmental approval and legal challenge risk in Australia under evolving 'Nature Positive' and biodiversity legislation

Tightening GHG/methane standards, carbon pricing (Safeguard Mechanism in Australia) and EU CBAM could raise compliance costs or affect demand for ammonia/LNG; net equity Scope 1&2 targets rely partly on carbon credits, an area of scrutiny and potential greenwashing litigation risk
Evolving US trade policy could affect Louisiana LNG costs despite Foreign-Trade Zone status mitigations
Large legacy asset base (NWS, Bass Strait, North Sea-style aging fields) carries escalating abandonment cost and regulatory compliance risk over time

macro.description: Earnings and cash flow are highly cyclical with Brent and Asian LNG benchmark prices; OPEC+ supply decisions and Chinese demand materially move outcomes

macro.risk: Long-run demand destruction from energy transition
macro.description: Accelerated renewables/EV adoption or faster-than-expected decarbonization could structurally reduce long-term oil and (to a lesser extent) LNG demand, pressuring terminal value of long-life assets
OECD projects global growth slowing to 2.9% in 2026 from 3.2% in 2025; softer industrial activity would reduce energy demand growth
Operations and growth projects span the US, Mexico, Senegal and Australia, exposing the company to sanctions, tariffs, and regional political instability

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global LNG markets are expected to grow strongly — Wood Mackenzie's base case projects ~60% (250 Mtpa) demand growth to 2035, driven by Asian energy security and coal-to-gas switching — while global oil demand growth is expected to moderate as economies decarbonize; more than 100 Mtpa of new LNG SPAs/HOAs were signed globally in 2025 (up from ~81 Mtpa in 2024), evidencing strong near-term contracting activity even as substantial new supply (216 Mtpa) is also under construction
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — Woodside's earnings are directly geared to Brent crude and LNG benchmark prices; FY2025 NPAT fell 24% YoY primarily on a 14.4% decline in average Brent price despite record production volumes
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — floating-rate debt/deposits and reliance on debt markets to fund multi-billion-dollar growth capex; investment-grade rating (Baa1/BBB+) helps but a downgrade would raise funding costs
key_input_costs: Labor and skilled engineering resources (tight during major project construction)
Steel, LNG modules and specialized equipment (Bechtel, Baker Hughes, Chart Louisiana LNG contractors)
Carbon credits/offsets (ACCUs, Verra, Gold Standard) used to meet emissions targets

recent_developments.event: CEO Meg O'Neill resigned to become CEO of BP effective April 2026; Liz Westcott (EVP & COO Australia) appointed Acting CEO
Woodside confirmed Liz Westcott as permanent CEO and Managing Director after a board succession process

FY2025 full-year results: record annual production of 198.8 MMboe, revenue of $12,984m (down 1%), NPAT of $2,718m (down 24% YoY on lower oil/LNG prices), underlying NPAT $2,649m, full-year dividend of 112 US cps at ~80% payout (top of 50-80% range), gearing 18.2% (within 10-20% target range)

Completed Louisiana LNG partnership agreements with Williams (10% interest in HoldCo, 80% interest and operatorship of Driftwood Pipeline) following the earlier Stonepeak infrastructure sell-down (40% of LALNG Infraco), reducing Woodside's capital intensity for the project to <60% of total capex

Completed divestment of Greater Angostura assets (Trinidad and Tobago) to Perenco; agreed to assume operatorship of Bass Strait assets from ExxonMobil (targeted completion H2 2026, later effective June 1, 2026), expected to deliver >US$60m of synergies

Took final investment decision (FID) on Louisiana LNG (total project cost $17.5bn, Woodside share $9.9bn), positioning the company as a two-basin (Pacific and Atlantic) global LNG supplier; targeting first LNG in 2029
First production achieved at Beaumont New Ammonia (Texas); lower-carbon ammonia production targeted H2 2026

H1 2026 results: NPAT up 27% YoY to $1.672bn, revenue up 13% to $7.446bn, underlying NPAT up 7% to $1.334bn; free cash flow up >150% YoY to $352m; Scarborough 98% complete (on budget, first cargo Q4 2026), Trion 64% complete, Louisiana LNG 28% complete; interim dividend raised to 57 US cps from 53 US cps
Signed non-binding MOU with Mexico's Pemex to explore further upstream/energy collaboration opportunities, building on the Trion partnership

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 results (25 August 2026) and FY2025 results (24 February 2026)

items.notes: Primarily Scarborough, Trion and Louisiana LNG; excludes final Beaumont New Ammonia completion payment
98% complete as of H1 2026 (on budget); first gas from offshore wells achieved subsequent to H1 2026
64% complete as of H1 2026; total project cost $7.2bn ($4.8bn Woodside share incl. PEMEX capital carry of ~$460m)
28% complete as of H1 2026; total project cost $17.5bn ($9.9bn Woodside share after Stonepeak/Williams sell-downs)
FY2025 final dividend paid at ~80% of H2 underlying NPAT (top of range); DRP remains suspended
18.2% at end of FY2025, within range; may temporarily exceed range to fund growth capex

items.target: 15% below starting base by end-2025 (achieved); 30% reduction by 2030
items.notes: 2025 target met via a mix of underlying operational performance and ~1,283 kt CO2-e of retired carbon credits

items.target: US$5 billion in new energy/lower-carbon services by 2030
items.notes: Cumulative spend reached $2.6bn by end-2025 (Beaumont, Neosmelt, CCS assessments); not formal guidance, subject to commercial/JV approvals

guidance.management_commentary: Acting/incoming CEO Liz Westcott has emphasized safe, reliable operations, cost discipline and delivery of near-term priorities amid major project completions; the FY2025 Chair's letter highlighted confidence that a larger, more resilient Woodside (post-BHP merger, post-Scarborough/Louisiana LNG) is well positioned through the energy transition, citing ~$11 billion of cumulative dividends paid to shareholders since the BHP merger. Management continues to frame LNG as a long-duration, structurally advantaged transition fuel versus coal, while acknowledging new-energy (ammonia/hydrogen) commercialization has progressed slower than anticipated due to cost, infrastructure and regulatory uncertainty.

bull_case: Three major growth projects (Scarborough, Trion, Louisiana LNG) are in execution and de-risked by strategic capital partners (Stonepeak, Williams, LNG Japan, PEMEX), with Scarborough imminent (Q4 2026 first cargo) — a step-change in production and cash flow is close at hand

Structural LNG demand tailwind (Wood Mackenzie forecasts ~60% demand growth to 2035) driven by Asian energy security and coal-to-gas switching, with Woodside well positioned via new long-term offtake contracts (4.7+ Mtpa signed in 2025) and a soon-to-be dual-basin (Pacific + Atlantic) LNG portfolio

Disciplined capital management with investment-grade credit ratings, gearing within a 10-20% target range, and a shareholder-friendly 50-80% payout policy that has already returned ~$11bn since the BHP merger

Record base-business execution — record 2025 production (198.8 MMboe), ~98% operated LNG reliability, and falling unit production costs ($7.8/boe) demonstrate strong operational competence supporting cash generation even in a lower price environment

Portfolio simplification/synergy capture through recent moves (Bass Strait operatorship, NWS/Chevron/Wheatstone swap, Greater Angostura divestment) that focus the Australian asset base and unlock incremental value
bear_case: Earnings remain highly geared to volatile oil and LNG prices; FY2025 NPAT fell 24% on a 14.4% Brent price decline despite record volumes, illustrating limited insulation from commodity cycles

Concentrated execution risk across three very large, multi-year capital projects simultaneously (Scarborough, Trion, Louisiana LNG); Louisiana LNG in particular has not yet locked in offtake for most of its volumes, and S&P has flagged a negative ratings outlook tied to a further required sell-down

Long-term decarbonization and demand-destruction risk for oil, and policy/permitting uncertainty (Australian environmental approvals, EU CBAM, evolving methane/carbon regulation) that could raise compliance costs or delay future projects (e.g., Browse)

New energy diversification (ammonia, hydrogen, CCUS) is commercializing more slowly than hoped, given cost, infrastructure and regulatory constraints, leaving the company still overwhelmingly reliant on fossil fuel volumes for revenue

Recent CEO transition (O'Neill to BP, Westcott newly confirmed) introduces leadership/execution continuity risk at precisely the moment several first-of-a-kind, multi-billion-dollar projects are reaching critical completion milestones
